set.n: Hermit Frank Van Arsdale's 'gold', Alamo Twp
set.tovw: Died penniless; the 500-diggers item is out-of-state filler; no find
set.st: An out-of-state filler item (Bloomsburg, Pa., 1907) says more than 500 people dug for hermit Frank Van Arsdale's hidden gold; no Michigan telling mentions gold or a search. He died March 1907 in a tenant house near Williams Station, 12 mi west of Kalamazoo, where he had once owned 200 acres. Local papers stress he died poor (ruined by signing friends' notes); neighbours auctioned his effects to pay for his burial in the Alamo cemetery. No hoard. Pin is on the family parcels, not a spot.
set.t: No hoard: record only. Access: private.

src: The Columbian (Bloomsburg, Pa.), 21 Mar 1907, p. 6 (newspapers.com 46488313): the 500-diggers filler

set.tovw: $7,000 unfound at his death July 1892; granary bean barrels were his bank
set.st: Eccentric Noah D. Keeler (b. 1812) of Liberty Twp died suddenly on 10 Jul 1892 on the farm he had worked about 58 years, 14 mi from Jackson, leaving no will; about $7,000 he was known to have 'can't be found'. His first wife once sold beans with several hundred dollars in gold in them, and he chased the buyer to Somerset Center and got it back; about 1890 bunco men took $1,300 in gold from a barrel of beans in his granary. 'It is believed the several thousand dollars … is hidden somewhere about. No one can buy beans now unless they are run through a coarse sieve first.' One telling. Pin is the farm house site, not the spot itself.

src: Detroit News, 28 Jul 1892, p. 8 'Eccentric Jackson Man Who Preferred Bean Barrels to National Banks' (newspapers.com 1377509190)
